newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends sharply up on LME gains.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends sharply up on LME gains.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended sharply up in active trading on Thursday due to heavy overnight gains on the London Metal Exchange (LME), traders said.
The most active June 1997 contract ended at 23,790 yuan ($2,867) per tonne, rising 540 yuan. It opened at 23,800 yuan, hitting an intraday high of 23,860 and a low of 23,760.
March rose 300 to 23,380, April 560 to 23,650, May 510 to 23,770, July 500 to 23,750 and August 530 to 23,780.
Combined volume rose sharply to 72,590 tonnes from 41,310.
Copper opened higher and moved at high levels for most of the session on heavy speculative buying boosted by overnight gains on the LME, traders said.
"Few investors dared to hold short positions on concerns about the potential for further rises, " one trader said.
Traders said firmer spot copper prices would continue to support the futures price.
They said they expected copper to rise further in the next few days.
Aluminium ended up following copper's trend. March rose 180 yuan to 15,880 yuan ($1,913) per tonne, April 200 to 16,200, May 210 to 16,550 and June 250 to 16,750.
Combined volume rose to 6,810 tonnes from 1,580.
